_doc: Per-class WORK-SIGNAL spec. Each class states (a) what the fixture must contain for the
package's real code path to be reachable, and (b) the predicate that decides DID-WORK.
Predicate operators, evaluated against the delta produced by delta.mjs and the run log:
created_all_of  : every regex must match >=1 entry in CREATED (root:rel form)
created_any_of  : >=1 regex must match >=1 CREATED entry
changed_any_of  : >=1 regex must match a PROJECT path changed in the window —
for a package whose effect lands outside its own store cell
cell_changed_any_of : as above but over the package's OWN CELL, for output that
lands beside the package rather than under its name
min_created     : CREATED entry count must be >= n (COUNTS DIRECTORIES — weak)
min_created_files : CREATED/MODIFIED regular-FILE count must be >= n
min_created_bytes : total bytes of CREATED/MODIFIED regular files must be >= n
content_nonce   : a CREATED/MODIFIED file matching `where` must CONTAIN the run nonce.
This is the ONLY operator a warm cache cannot satisfy, because the
nonce is generated per run and cannot pre-exist. Prefer it wherever
the class admits it.
log_match       : the combined stdout+stderr must match
PREFER FILES AND BYTES OVER PATH COUNTS. `min_created` is satisfied by a DIRECTORY,
and a downloader whose fetch is refused leaves exactly one: its empty staging dir.
Five of the 44 downloaders the first macOS corpus scored as surviving the jail were
false passes on that operator alone.
STRENGTH is recorded per class and is not decoration: a verdict built on a weak signal
must be labelled weak in the corpus output, or the corpus overstates its own confidence.

fixture: No project files needed. The hazard is the opposite of a missing input: node-gyp
packages increasingly ship or fetch a PREBUILD and skip compilation entirely, which is
a bail-out of the path we mean to test. Force source compilation with
npm_config_build_from_source=true in the install env, and assert the .o evidence below.
why: The .o requirement is what separates COMPILED from DOWNLOADED. A prebuild-install
fallback produces build/Release/*.node with no object files at all, so an artifact-only
predicate would score a skipped compile as a successful one.

fixture: Cold download cache, and that cache directory MUST be inside a snapshot root (usually
$HOME or the package's own cache dir) or the download leaves no observable trace.
Set npm_config_build_from_source=false so the download path is the one under test.
why: No nonce is possible: the artifact is an upstream-fixed binary, so its content cannot
carry a per-run marker. The signal therefore rests entirely on CREATED-in-window plus a
verified-cold cache. State that dependency wherever the number is cited.
The byte floor is what stops a truncated or zero-length `.node` from reading as a
download: no real N-API addon is 16 KiB. It is a FLOOR, not the evidence — the evidence
is the cross-arm size ratio the aggregate applies on top.

fixture: Cold per-package download cache, inside a snapshot root. Many of these consult a
*_SKIP_DOWNLOAD / *_BINARY_PATH env var; the env must be verified free of them, since
an inherited skip flag is a silent bail-out that scores as a pass.
why: Same no-nonce limitation as the prebuilt class, so the artifact itself has to carry the
signal. The old predicate was `min_created: 1` over any created path, with the size
corroboration left as 'checkable post hoc' — which nobody ever checked. Five of the 44
downloaders the first macOS corpus scored as surviving the jail were false passes, each
satisfying it with something that is not a download: three bin symlinks the LINKER made
inside the cell (`azure-functions-core-tools`, `chromium`, `cldr-data` — 601 MB, an
entire Chromium.app and 13,296 locale files missing respectively), an empty staging
DIRECTORY created just before the fetch was refused (`@go-task/cli`, whose own log reads
`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND github.com`), and nub's own 117-byte jail-home scratch, which
exists only in the confined arm. Requiring FILES and BYTES makes all four shapes
unsatisfiable; the bin-link and scratch shapes are additionally refused at attribution.
64 KiB is a floor below any real downloaded binary or archive, not a measurement — the
measurement is the cross-arm size ratio the aggregate applies on top.

fixture: The generator's INPUT must exist in the project — for Prisma a schema.prisma with a
generator block and a datasource block. Without it the postinstall exits 0 having done
nothing, which is the archetypal false pass this whole method exists to catch.
The schema MUST embed the run nonce (e.g. a model named NubProbe<RUNID>).
why: Content-derivation is unforgeable. A generated client carrying a model name that was
invented for this run cannot have come from a cache, a sibling arm, or a previous run.
This is the only class where the work-signal is immune to every cache trap by
construction rather than by hygiene.

fixture: A REAL .git directory — `git init` plus at least one commit, since some installers
check for a valid repository rather than the directory's mere existence. Also ensure
the fixture does not set core.hooksPath already, and that HUSKY / lefthook skip vars
are absent from the environment.
why: The effect lands in the project tree, which makes this class the sharpest probe of the
project-file grant axis: under a jail that grants no project access it must fail, and a
pass would mean the grant is wider than believed.

fixture: Nothing. The class has no input requirement, which is itself the problem.
why: HONEST GAP. This class produces no filesystem effect by design, so the tree delta is
empty on both the real and the bail path and cannot separate them. The only candidates
are an attempted-connect (needs a syscall trace, unavailable unprivileged on macOS) and
an exact stdout string (author-controlled, changes between versions, and absent when the
package detects a non-TTY or CI). This class is reported as UNSIGNALLED rather than
given a predicate that would manufacture false confidence.

fixture: Cold cache; and check for an 'already configured' short-circuit, which is the bail-out
shape for this class.
why: Heterogeneous class with no common artifact. Treated as ACTED-only: it can be separated
from NEVER-RAN but not verified to have done its specific job, so it must never be
counted in a 'succeeded' figure without a per-package predicate written by hand.
FILES, not paths: `argon2` scored a pass here on six `.bin` symlinks the linker made,
having produced nothing of its own.

_doc: A PER-PACKAGE PREDICATE REPLACES ITS CLASS PREDICATE OUTRIGHT, keyed by `name@version`
or by bare `name`. It exists for packages whose class is right about WHAT THEY DO and
wrong about HOW IT IS OBSERVED — not as a place to soften a predicate a package fails.
The bar for adding one: the class predicate must be unsatisfiable BY CONSTRUCTION for
this package, and the replacement must name a specific artifact that only the real code
path produces. An entry that merely widens a predicate until the package passes is the
false-pass machinery this whole file exists to prevent, wearing a different hat.

why: Classed `codegen`, whose predicate is `content_nonce` — unsatisfiable here BY
CONSTRUCTION, because msw copies a FIXED service-worker file and no per-run nonce can
ever appear in it. The postinstall's entire observable effect is that one file, written
into the project at the path `msw.workerDirectory` names, so the file IS the signal.
It also lands OUTSIDE msw's own store cell, which is why per-package attribution saw
nothing and scored NEVER-RAN in both arms.
Measured on the isolated pair: created in A0 and in PROD alike — msw works under the jail.
Same construction problem as msw: `codegen` by class, fixed content in fact. Its
postinstall copies 22 `@types/deck.gl*` trees into its own cell beside itself, which no
path rule can claim as `own-package-dir` — they read as dependency links — so the
package scored DID-WORK-AND-FAILED while doing exactly its job.
Only in-window entries count, and the linker finishes before the window opens, so a hit
is the script's work. Measured on the isolated pair: 64 such entries in A0 and in PROD
alike — it works under the jail.
Classed `binary-downloader`, and it DOES download — 38,059,875 B of `mac.dmg`, byte-
identical to the unconfined arm once its egress grant landed. It then dies at
`hdiutil attach mac.dmg -> Device not configured`, because attaching a disk image needs
diskarbitrationd and Seatbelt refuses it. So the deliverable, `bin/HandbrakeCLI`, is
ABSENT under the jail and present without it.
The class predicate scored this a PASS and the cross-arm size ratio did not catch it:
the .dmg is 36% of the extracted binary, well clear of the 0.1 gate. That is the gate's
documented limit — it scales TOTAL created bytes, so a large intermediate can carry a
run whose actual product never appeared. Naming the binary is the only signal that
distinguishes them.
Measured 2026-07-31, macOS arm64, both shards it appears in (break1, default7).
